questions.question_text:
A tractor is bought for $\$96\,000$ and depreciates at $22\%$ p.a.
What is its salvage value after $3$ years, to the nearest cent?

options.why: This is the total depreciation $V_{0}-S$, not the salvage value asked for.
Used $(1+r)^{n}$ instead of $(1-r)^{n}$, growing the value instead of shrinking it.
Subtracted $22\%$ of $\$96\,000$ as a flat $\$21\,120$ three times, treating the loss as constant.

questions.question_text:
A courier van costs $\$54\,000$ and depreciates at $30\%$ p.a.
By how much has it depreciated in total after $2$ years?

options.why: This is the salvage value left, not the amount of value lost.
Subtracted $30\%$ of $\$54\,000$ as a flat $\$16\,200$ each year, treating the loss as constant.
Used $(1+r)^{n}$ and then subtracted the initial value, so the sign of $r$ was wrong.

questions.question_text:
Business equipment depreciating at $25\%$ p.a. has a salvage value of $\$17\,718.75$ after $4$ years.
What was its purchase price, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Multiplied by $(1+r)^{n}$, using a growth multiplier instead of dividing by the decay multiplier.
Multiplied by $(1-r)^{n}$ instead of dividing, shrinking the value a second time.
Divided by $(1-r)$ once only, using $n=1$ instead of $n=4$.

questions.question_text:
A bakery oven bought for $\$18\,000$ is worth $\$14\,580$ after $2$ years.
What is the annual depreciation rate?

options.why: Divided the total loss of $\$3420$ by $\$18\,000$ and halved it, treating the loss as constant.
Gave the total percentage lost over both years instead of the rate per year.
Gave the multiplier $1-r=0.9$ as a percentage instead of the rate $r$.

questions.question_text:
A forklift bought for $\$50\,000$ depreciates at $10\%$ p.a.
Find how long it takes to depreciate to $\$32\,805$, to the nearest year.

options.why: Stopped at $n=3$, when $50000(0.9)^3=\$36\,450$, which is still above the target.
Went one year beyond the exact target: $50000(0.9)^5=\$29\,524.50$.
Used $0.1$ as the remaining-value multiplier instead of $0.9$, giving $\$5000$ after one year and choosing the wrong time.
Read the value at the end of year $1$ instead of the purchase price at year $0$.
Read the value at the end of year $2$ instead of the purchase price at year $0$.
Subtracted the year-$1$ value from the initial value, giving the first year's depreciation instead of the purchase price.

questions.solution_text:
The purchase price is the value at $n=0$.
The graph shows $V_0=\$32\,000$.

questions.question_text:
The value of a printing press is given by $14\,000(0.83)^{6}$. Assume annual depreciation periods.
Which statement describes this asset?

options.text: A $\$14\,000$ press depreciating at $17\%$ p.a. for $6$ years
A $\$14\,000$ press depreciating at $83\%$ p.a. for $6$ years
options.why: Read the multiplier $0.83$ as the depreciation rate itself instead of solving $1-r=0.83$.

options.text: A $\$14\,000$ press growing in value at $17\%$ p.a. for $6$ years
options.why: Found $r=0.17$ correctly but treated $(0.83)^{6}$ as a growth factor, so the direction of the change is reversed.

options.text: A $\$14\,000$ press growing in value at $83\%$ p.a. for $6$ years
options.why: Made both slips: read $0.83$ straight off as the rate and also took the bracket to be a growth multiplier.

questions.solution_text:
$1-r=0.83$
$r=0.17$
The expression is the value of a $\$14\,000$ press depreciating at $17\%$ p.a. for $6$ years.

questions.question_text:
An asset costs $\$20\,000$ and depreciates by $20\%$ per half year.
What is its salvage value after $2$ years?

options.why: Used $n=2$ instead of $n=4$, counting years rather than half-year periods.
Calculated $20000-8192$, giving total depreciation instead of salvage value.
Subtracted $20\%$ of the initial value four times, treating each half year's dollar loss as constant.

questions.question_text:
A quarry crusher costs $\$32\,000$ and depreciates at $25\%$ p.a.
Find how long it takes to depreciate by a total of $\$18\,500$, to the nearest year.

options.why: Treated $\$18\,500$ as the salvage value rather than the total loss; the value after two years is $\$18\,000$.
Went one year beyond the target; after four years the total loss is $32000-10125=\$21\,875$.
Used $0.25$ as the remaining-value multiplier instead of $0.75$, giving a first-year loss of $\$24\,000$.
